narrative:

The strongest reason was your third-year class rank: you were in the lowest decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile. This was the most influential factor and pushed the prediction toward failure. Your first-year class rank was the second most important factor; it was also in the lowest decile, compared with an accepted-student average near the sixth decile, and it also pushed toward failure. Your undergraduate GPA was the third most important factor. At 3.00 it was slightly below the accepted average of 3.23, but in this prediction it worked modestly in your favor, pushing toward passing.

To improve your next application, focus on demonstrating stronger academic readiness: seek advising about your low class ranks, build a clear study and support plan for bar preparation, consider retaking the LSAT if you can improve it, and apply to programs that review the full record. Ask admissions offices for feedback and address the weak spots directly.
